questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle with centre O. C is point on the circle in the minor sector. If ∠ABO = 50°, then what is the degree measure of ∠ACB ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ABO = 50°

Concept used:

The sum of a pair of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180° (supplementary).

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is twice the angle subtended at the circumference

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15c4a91d73210e17a719ad4771a79ea7a4cc4619cb599c7b8844e803a1132e22.png] 

OA = OB = radius of the circle

So, ∠ABO = ∠BAO = 50°

So, ∠AOB = 180° - (50° + 50°)

⇒ ∠AOB = 180° - 100°

⇒ ∠AOB = 80°

Let A and B meet at point D in the major sector

Now,

∠ADB = 80°/2 = 40°

ACBD is a cyclic quadrilateral 

So, ∠ACB = 180° - 40°

⇒ ∠ACB = 140°

**∴ The measure of ∠ACB is 140°.**

questions.question:
In the given figure, If ∠RPS = 25°, the value of ∠ROS is_______. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e99572eb2028a9907caf5319cd46b9705f4967a67d871a58decd5f7add8b891.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4e99572eb2028a9907caf5319cd46b9705f4967a67d871a58decd5f7add8b891.png] 

∠RPS = 25°

∠S = ∠R = 90° [Tangent of a circle is perpendicular to the Radius]

**Concept used:**

Sum of all the angles of quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculations:**

According to the question,

in quadrilateral OSPR,

⇒ ∠ P + ∠ S + ∠ O + ∠ R = 360° 

⇒ 25° + 90° + ∠ O + 90° = 360° 

⇒ ∠ ROS = 360° - 205° = 155°

**∴ The value of ∠ROS is 155°. **

questions.question: RA and RB are two tangents from a common point ‘R’ outside the circle with centre ‘O’, having a radius of 6 cm. If ∠ARB = 70°, find the measure of the angle AOB.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius = 6 cm 

∠ARB = 70°

**Concept Used:**

Sum of the angles of a quadrilateral is 360°

The angle between the radius and the tangent of a circle is 90°

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10ad6bb1d49d4fe270d3670c70f4d782d20f026a7bd6de419bce1ecbd8bccc13.png] **

⇒ The 4 points A, B, R and O make a quadrilateral

⇒ ∠RAO = ∠RBO = 90°

⇒ ∠RAO + ∠AOB + ∠RBO + ∠ARB = 360°

⇒ 90° + ∠AOB + 90° + 70° = 360°

⇒ ∠AOB = 360° – 250° = 110°

**∴ The value of ∠AOB is 110°.**

questions.question: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. Then what is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The Radii of the two circles are 18 cm and 12 cm.

The length of their common chord is 16 cm.

**Concept used:**

A line that is drawn perpendicular to the chord from the center of a circle always bisects the chord.

H² = B² + P²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91913594aa8fb525717bcc6cc8c7bef2131e66d3cf8782429636be650191b2d3.png] 

At first join O, P and A 

Now, OBA is a right angle triangle and PBA is also a right angle triangle.

Length of AB = AC/2 = 16/2 = 8 cm.

Again, OB² = 18² – 8² = 260

⇒ OB = √260 = 2√65 

And BP² = 12² – 8² = 80

⇒ BP = 4√5

Now distance between their centres is OP = OB + BP

⇒ OP = 2√65 + 4√5

⇒ OP = 2√5(2 + √13)

**∴ Distance (in cm) between their centers is 2√5(2 + √13)**

questions.question:
In the given figure, chords AB and CD intersect each other at point L. Find CL.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d43a72ef5a5193a6690c8015c2045ba7a42a6d6d73372fbd67ae617827d3681.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AL = 8 cm

BL = 3 cm

DL = 6 cm

**Concept Used:**

CL × LD = BL × LA

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d43a72ef5a5193a6690c8015c2045ba7a42a6d6d73372fbd67ae617827d3681.png] 

⇒ Let the length of CL be x cm.

⇒ Putting the given values in the formula,

⇒ x×6=8×3

⇒ x=(24)/(6)=4cm

**Hence, the length of CL is 4 cm.**

questions.question:
In the following figure, if PT = 12 cm and PB = 24 cm, then find AB.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d3164ae81478d7af057942b5390ae9a0b0cb5ed5f638e205114d8de06e78430.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d3164ae81478d7af057942b5390ae9a0b0cb5ed5f638e205114d8de06e78430.png] 

**Formula Used:**

From the tangent theorem,

PT² = PA x PB

**Calculations:**

⇒ Here, PT = 12 cm

⇒ PB = 24 cm

Now put the value of PT and PB 

⇒ PT2 = PA x PB

⇒ 12² = PA x 24

⇒ PA = 144 / 24 = 6 cm

As we know,

⇒ PB = PA + AB

⇒ AB = PB - PA = 24 - 6 = 18 cm

⇒ **Hence, The value of AB is 18 cm.**

questions.question: A 9-cm-long perpendicular is drawn from the center of circle to a chord of length 24 cm. The radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
Given: 

A 9-cm-long perpendicular is drawn from the centre of circle to a chord of length 24 cm.

Concept used:

Perpendicular drawn from centre of circle to the chord bisects the chord

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aca3a24f9de4bcaae7c00a7a85efdee245bd848b29c6497949dfbb2fd6cec909.png] 

⇒ AM = MB = 24/2 = 12 cm

In Right triangle AMO,

AO² = OM2 + AM² = 9² + 12² = 225

⇒ AM² = 225

⇒ AM = 15 cm

questions.question: A circle touches the side BC of ΔABC at P and also touches AB and AC produced at Q and R, respectively. If the perimeter of ΔABC = 14.1 cm, then the length (in cm) of AQ will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A circle touches the side BC of ΔABC at P and also touches AB and AC produced at Q and R, respectively.

The perimeter of ΔABC = 14.1 cm

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d640fd4754b17e3fff2873580c35de8c0b065af3e724b8dd682f86c9334b20a7.png] 

AQ = AR [Tangents]

BP = BQ [Tangents]

CP = CR [Tangents]

Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BP + CP + AC

⇒ 14.1 = AB + BQ + CR + AC

⇒ 14.1 = AQ + AR

⇒ 14.1 = AQ + AQ

⇒ 14.1 = 2AQ

⇒ AQ = (14.1/2) cm

⇒ AQ = 7.05 cm

**∴ The length of AQ is 7.05 cm**

questions.question: Two circle touch each other externally. The distance between their centres is 14 cm. If the radius of one circle is 8 cm, then the radius of the other circle is:
questions.solution:
**Given**:

Two circles touch each other externally. 

The distance between their centres = 14 cm.

The radius of one circle = 8 cm

**Concept used:**

When two circles touch each other externally then the distance between their centres is given by the sum of their radii.

**Formula used:**

Distance between their centres = Radius of Ist circle + Radius of 2ⁿd circle

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/058ec9c5984a5019434e29c680fe2ed6053989e8f183a31d3f0082c77519154c.png] 

Let r be the radius of the 2ⁿd circle.

According to the question

⇒ 14 = 8 + r

⇒ r = (14 – 8) cm

⇒ r = 6 cm

**∴ The radius of the other circle is 6 cm**

questions.question: AB is 12 cm long chord of a circle with centre O and radius 10 cm. The tangents at A and B intersect at P. What is the length of OP?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 12 cm

Radius = 10 cm

The tangents at A and B intersect at P.

**Concept used:**

**AAA similarity:** If all three angles in one triangle are the same as the corresponding angles in the other, then the triangles are similar.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4342df0d3a229c6831f5e01077e9458c5db4f4381e9dd4d109c1a502860a2803.png] 

AB is the chord of the circle with centre O

Now,

OP ⊥ AB

So, OP bisects AB

AL = BL = 6 cm

Also,

OL = √(OA)² – (AL)²

⇒ OL = √(10)² – (6)²

⇒ OL = √100 – 36

⇒ OL = √64

⇒ OL = 8 cm

Now,

In ΔOAP and ΔOLA

∠OAP = ∠OLA

OA = OB = 10 cm (Radius)

OL = OL [Common]

So, ΔOAP ~ ΔOLA 

⇒ OP/OA = OA/OL [Corresponding sides are proportional]

⇒ OP/10 = 10/8

⇒ 8 OP = 100

⇒ OP = (100/8) cm

⇒ OP = 12.5 cm

**∴ The length of OP is 12.5 cm**
